title: Private planning bootstrap
description:
Private planning/bootstrap epic for the auxide kernel (Graph → Plan → Runtime). Tracks kernel-level work: the cross-crate integration gate (auxide-b7x), first-class runtime control for external nodes (auxide-cpr.1), and any future kernel features. Children own their own DoD. This epic is the audit parent; it closes only after every child has a populated acceptance + design and is independently completable.

## Success Criteria
- Every child bead (auxide-b7x, auxide-cpr.1) has non-empty acceptance and design (verified via `bd show <id>`).
- The cross-crate integration gate (auxide-b7x) is green and repeatable via a single command.
- The runtime control contract (auxide-cpr.1) is documented and tested.
design: PLAN: Tracker only — no code here. After children close, re-run the full kernel + cross-crate gate and close this epic last.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — epic closes only when:
1. Every child bead (e.g., auxide-b7x) has non-empty `--acceptance` and `--design` (verified via `bd show <id>`).
2. The cross-crate integration gate (auxide-b7x) is green and repeatable via a single command.

title: Design first-class runtime control for external DSP nodes
description: Define the control-plane contract needed so external nodes from auxide-dsp can be modulated at runtime without rebuilding the graph. Cover plan representation, RT-safe parameter transport, and host/runtime control APIs.

title: Implement RT-safe runtime control plane for external nodes
description: Replace the shipped snapshot's legacy-only runtime with a split runtime/control model that can execute external nodes and accept live parameter changes without rebuilding the graph. Keep the implementation RT-safe and avoid per-block allocation in the audio path.
acceptance_criteria: runtime exposes a control-capable handle/core split or equivalent RT-safe control surface; external nodes execute in the runtime; live parameter updates reach running graphs; no per-block Vec allocation remains in the RT path

title: Add render_offline for RuntimeHandle (new architecture)
description: The legacy render_offline() works with the old Runtime but doesn't support control messages. The new RuntimeHandle/RuntimeCore architecture supports control messages but has no offline rendering helper. Add render_offline_handle(handle: &mut RuntimeHandle, frames: usize) -> Result<Vec<f32>, &'static str> so offline tests and demos can drive external nodes via the control queue.
acceptance_criteria:
1. render_offline_handle exists in rt.rs and takes &mut RuntimeHandle
2. It renders N frames by looping handle.process_block()
3. It handles partial final blocks correctly
4. cargo test --all-features passes with -D warnings
5. The function is documented with doc comments
close_reason: render_offline_handle(handle, frames) added to rt.rs. Mirrors legacy render_offline but works with RuntimeHandle/RuntimeCore, supporting control messages. All tests pass.

title: Add external node support to graph and plan
description: Bring the shipped snapshot's graph/compiler layer up to the required external-node model. Add a NodeType::External path, add_external_node(), and the plan/compiler handling needed so external DSP node definitions can exist in compiled graphs.
acceptance_criteria: graph.rs defines NodeType::External and add_external_node(); plan compilation accepts external nodes; tests cover external node graph construction and compile ordering
notes: Closed after syncing the saved graph/planner/runtime repair to disk and validating with cargo test --workspace. External node support is now present in graph.rs/plan.rs/rt.rs and the workspace test suite passes.

title: Verify full-suite end-to-end compile and test across all four crates
description:
Verify full-suite end-to-end compile and test across all four crates (auxide, auxide-dsp, auxide-io, auxide-midi), which are linked by path dependencies. Today there is no single repeatable command that proves the whole stack builds, lints, and tests together, and no cross-crate smoke test that proves a DSP graph actually renders through the kernel and is drivable by the MIDI bridge.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. A single script `verify_all.sh` cd's into each of the four crates and runs `cargo build`, `cargo test`, and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`; all exit 0 on a clean checkout.
2. Every crate is warning-clean under `-D warnings`.
3. NEW cross-crate smoke test: build a SynthBuilder graph (auxide-dsp) → RuntimeCore::new_with_channels (auxide) → render offline → assert non-zero; and construct MidiBridgeConfig + exercise VoiceAllocator/VoicePool on NoteOn/NoteOff (no real device needed).
4. README documents the `verify_all.sh` command as the integration gate.

## Design
A. Write `verify_all.sh` looping the four crates with build/test/clippy.
B. Add cross-crate integration test using SynthBuilder + RuntimeCore + render_offline.
C. Add a MIDI-path test building MidiBridgeConfig + allocator.
D. Wire command into README. Run; iterate.
design:
PLAN:
A. Write `verify_all.sh` looping `for c in auxide auxide-dsp auxide-io auxide-midi; do (cd $c && cargo build && cargo test && cargo clippy -- -D warnings) || exit 1; done`.
B. Add a cross-crate integration test that uses `auxide_dsp::builders::SynthBuilder` + `auxide::rt::RuntimeCore::new_with_channels` + `auxide::rt::render_offline` (legacy Runtime) to render and assert non-zero; run it from the crate that depends on both (auxide-midi or auxide-dsp).
C. For the MIDI path, add a test that builds `MidiBridgeConfig::default()` and exercises `VoiceAllocator`/`VoicePool` on NoteOn/NoteOff (no real device needed).
D. Wire the command into README's CI/verification section.
E. Run the script; iterate until all four crates are green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. A single script `verify_all.sh` (committed at repo root or in auxide) cd's into each of the four crates and runs `cargo build`, `cargo test`, and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`; all exit 0 on a clean checkout.
2. `cargo clippy --workspace` semantics reproduced per crate: every crate is warning-clean under `-D warnings`.
3. NEW cross-crate smoke test (in auxide-midi/tests or auxide-dsp/tests): build a SynthBuilder graph (auxide-dsp) → RuntimeCore::new_with_channels (auxide) → render offline N blocks → assert non-zero output; and construct MidiBridgeConfig + a mocked/no-device MidiToAudioBridge path proving the control flow compiles and the voice pool allocates on note_on.
4. README documents the `verify_all.sh` command as the integration gate.
notes: TECHNICAL CONTEXT: auxide-dsp is now at v0.2.0. Check Cargo.toml dependencies in auxide-midi and auxide-io to ensure they reference compatible versions. The auxide-dsp crate has been restructured (legacy DspNode modules deleted, builders now wire edges, RT test uses counting allocator).

title: Design first-class runtime control for external DSP nodes
description:
Design first-class runtime control for external DSP nodes. The auxide kernel already provides the control plane: the ControlMsg enum and canonical `PARAM_*` indices in src/control.rs, the `NodeDef::set_param`/`gate` trait methods, and `RuntimeCore::apply_control_msg` routing in src/rt.rs. This bead formalizes and tests that contract so ANY external node (e.g., auxide-dsp) can be driven live from the main thread without breaking RT safety. It is the producer side consumed by dsp-4y9.1 and midi-u4h.1.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `cargo test -p auxide` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide -- -D warnings` clean.
2. `control.rs` documents the canonical `PARAM_*` index contract and `apply_control_msg` routes every semantic ControlMsg (SetFrequency/SetFilterCutoff/SetFilterResonance/SetDetune/SetWaveform/SetPan/TriggerGate/AllNotesOff/Mute/Reset) onto the matching NodeDef method.
3. NEW test `apply_control_msg_routes_all`: a recording TestExternalNode (records set_param idx + gate calls) is driven by each ControlMsg variant; assert every variant reaches the expected NodeDef call.
4. NEW test `param_index_contract`: `SetParam{param_idx: PARAM_CUTOFF, ..}` reaches `node.set_param(PARAM_CUTOFF, ..)` (proves canonical indices are the single contract).

## Design
A. In control.rs add a doc comment block enumerating the canonical PARAM_* indices and meaning.
B. In rt.rs add `#[cfg(test)] apply_control_msg_routes_all` using a recording TestExternalNode; send each ControlMsg and assert.
C. Add `param_index_contract` asserting PARAM_CUTOFF passthrough.
D. Reference this contract from dsp-4y9.1 and midi-u4h.1. Iterate until green.
design:
PLAN:
A. In control.rs, add a doc comment block enumerating the canonical PARAM_* indices and their meaning (single source of truth).
B. In rt.rs add `#[cfg(test)] apply_control_msg_routes_all` using a TestExternalNode that records (param_idx, value) on set_param and on/off on gate; send each ControlMsg and assert.
C. Add `param_index_contract` asserting the PARAM_CUTOFF passthrough.
D. Reference this contract from dsp-4y9.1 (consumer) and midi-u4h.1 (producer). Iterate until green.
acceptance_criteria:
GATED EXIT — all must hold:
1. `cargo test -p auxide` green; `cargo clippy -p auxide -- -D warnings` clean.
2. `control.rs` documents the canonical `PARAM_*` index contract and `apply_control_msg` routes every semantic ControlMsg (SetFrequency/SetFilterCutoff/SetFilterResonance/SetDetune/SetWaveform/SetPan/TriggerGate/AllNotesOff/Mute/Reset) onto the matching NodeDef method.
3. NEW test `apply_control_msg_routes_all`: a recording TestExternalNode (records set_param idx + gate calls) is driven by each ControlMsg variant; assert every variant reaches the expected NodeDef call.
4. NEW test `param_index_contract`: `SetParam{param_idx: PARAM_CUTOFF, ..}` reaches `node.set_param(PARAM_CUTOFF, ..)` (proves the canonical indices are the single contract).

title: Create offline ROMpler demo producing .wav proof of full stack
description:
Create an example (examples/rompler_demo.rs) that:
1. Loads or generates a sample (Arc<Vec<f32>>)
2. Builds the ROMpler graph via build_rompler_graph() from auxide-midi
3. Creates a RuntimeCore with control channels
4. Sends TriggerGate + SetFrequency via control queue to start a voice
5. Renders ~1 second of audio offline using render_offline_handle
6. Writes result to rompler_demo.wav via hound

This proves the entire stack works end-to-end: sample → Sampler node → ADSR envelope → Mix → SVF filter → OutputSink, driven by control messages from the lock-free queue.
acceptance_criteria:
1. examples/rompler_demo.rs exists and compiles
2. Running 'cargo run --example rompler_demo' produces rompler_demo.wav
3. The .wav is non-silent (contains audible audio)
4. All 4 crates compile clean
5. cargo test --all-features passes with -D warnings for all crates
close_reason: examples/rompler_demo.rs created. Builds ROMpler graph, triggers note via control queue, renders via render_offline_handle, writes rompler_demo.wav. Peak=0.97, RMS=0.50 — real audio output.
